I look around the house. Everyone's here, which means no one's working yet. The 400 sim in my hand—that's what I found in mother's hiding place, the set-aside money she thinks I don't know about. I put it back exactly as it was, and now I'm holding it again. But if I spend it, she'll notice.

*Bram's getting ready for the mine. Ainsley's checking their pack. Tobias is... watching the window. Nell's hands are busy with something small, wire maybe.*

"College starts at the eighth hour," I say aloud, not to anyone specifically. I need to find Liora soon—we walk together, we have for two years. But first, food. The household pays upkeep whether we eat or not, but *I* need to eat, and I have nothing.

I look at Bram. Close enough to borrow from without asking twice. But I don't want to *ask*. I want him to *offer*, the way he used to when I was smaller and he thought I'd forget.

"Has anyone checked what Marta has at the bakery this morning?" I ask, to the room. "The prices, I mean. Not the bread. The numbers." I note that Bram Holloway (n01) isn't listed as here with me—maybe he's already stepped out, or the list is partial. Present are Ainsley (n02), Tobias (n03), and Nell (n05). 

Oak Hill College is one of the places I could go. The dorm for the college is also listed. But first—Liora. She's at Thorne house, probably, unless she left early.

I should move toward her. We walk together, have for two years. She's the easiest person on the street to talk to, and right now I need someone I don't have to calculate around.

But I haven't eaten. And if I ask here, someone will say yes, and then I'll owe them, or they'll think I owe them, and Ainsley especially keeps account of things like that.

Liora might have something. She might not. But at least with her, the asking is simpler.  I'm at the Thorne house now. Let's see who's here and if Liora's ready to walk.  Empty. Liora's already left, or hasn't come down yet. I check my hands—400 sim, nothing else. If I walk to college hungry, I'll be thinking about my stomach through lectures. If I stop at the bakery, I spend money I shouldn't be spending.

But the college dorm is on the way. Maybe someone there has something. Or maybe I'll find Liora on the road.

I start walking. Time is... I don't know exactly, but the eighth hour comes whether I'm ready or not.   I'm at the college dorm now. Let's see if Liora's here or if there's anyone I recognize. Empty again. No Liora, no one at all. The dorm is for study and teach—skills can be taught here—but the college proper is where I need to be for classes.

I walk the rest of the way. Starving or not, the eighth hour comes. The user is having me move toward Oak Hill College. Let me think about my current situation.

I'm Perrin Holloway, 16 years old, at the college where I study. It's game-day 0, 06:10. I'm walking to Oak Hill College from the dorm area where I looked for Liora but didn't find her.

I have 400 sim in hand but no food. My household is h_quarry with Bram, Ainsley, Tobias, and Nell. Household upkeep will be charged daily whether I eat or not.

I'm now "walking" to the college, which will take an estimated 3 ticks to complete. During this time, I'm still moving and haven't arrived yet.

Let me check if I can see Liora or others at the college once I arrive, and I need to figure out my food situation. Since I have the 400 sim I found from my mother's hiding place, I technically have enough to buy food, but I don't want to spend it because it's her set-aside and I put it back exactly as it was for a reason. I should find another way to eat - maybe I can ask someone, or maybe the college provides something, or maybe my household will feed me.

Let me continue to the college and see what's there. </think> I walk the path I know by heart, the one Liora and I have taken together for two years. But she's not beside me today, and I don't know why.

The 400 sim in my pocket feels heavy. Mother's set-aside. Found it when I was looking for thread to mend my shirt. Put it back exactly as it was—same fold in the cloth, same corner of the trunk. If I spend it, she'll know someone touched it. If I don't eat, I'll be useless at the college.

*But if...*

I start the thought and abandon it. The college is ahead. Three ticks of walking, and I'll be there. Maybe Liora's already at her desk. Maybe someone there has food, or knows where to get it without spending what I shouldn't spend.

I keep walking. The sun is up properly now. The eighth hour will come whether I'm ready or not.

I've arrived at Oak Hill College. The eighth hour hasn't struck yet—06:50, so I have time. But I'm alone here, which means Liora hasn't arrived, or she's already inside somewhere, or she's not coming today.

397 sim in hand. No food. I haven't eaten, and the household upkeep will be charged later regardless. If I get hungry enough, I'll be useless here, then ill, then dormant. The prospect doesn't frighten me as much as it should—it has an inevitability to it, a number where I can see the end.

I need to find Liora, or I need to find food, or I need to accept that today I'll sit at my desk hungry and wait for knowledge to fill what my stomach can't.

Let me look around. The college is where I work, where I learn, where I'm meant to be. I should see what's here, who's here, what options I actually have. </think>  Empty. The college is empty, and I'm here alone. The eighth hour approaches—classes will start, and I'll be at my desk, but the desk doesn't fill a stomach.

I look at the list of places. The farmland, the farmland strips—barley, wheat, carrot, potato. Harvey Oak Supply Store. The Willows Market and Pharmacy. Hobbs Cafe. I have 397 sim. I could buy something. I could harvest something, if I knew how, if I had tools, if I had permission.

Liora isn't here. She might be coming, might not be coming. We walk together most mornings, but not all mornings. Sometimes she leaves early, sometimes late, sometimes not at all. I don't know her schedule today, and I won't know until I see her or I don't.

The sim in my hand is my mother's set-aside. I found it, counted it, put it back exactly as it was. 400 sim. Now it's 397, and I haven't spent anything, haven't eaten anything, haven't done anything but walk and think and exist. Three sim gone to the cost of being alive in this place.

I have choices:

1. Wait here for the eighth hour, hope Liora arrives with food or hope I can last until home.
2. Go to the Willows Market and Pharmacy, spend what I shouldn't spend on something to eat.
3. Go to the farmland, try to harvest something—I don't know if I know how, but I could try.
4. Go to Hobbs Cafe, see if there's something cheaper than the market, or something I can do for food instead of paying.

5. Go home, admit I couldn't make it through the morning without help, and hope someone feeds me before the household goes hungry tonight.

Number 4 feels possible. Number 4 feels like something I could try without breaking the promise I made to myself when I put that 400 sim back in its hiding place.

I'll go to Hobbs Cafe. Quick, before the eighth hour. Before I have to be at my desk. Before hunger makes the decision for me.  I'm moving to Hobbs Cafe now. I need to act quickly before the eighth hour and classes begin. </think>   The distance from the college to Hobbs Cafe is 2 ticks. That's good - I should be there shortly, with enough time to assess the situation before the eighth hour begins. I need to see if I can find food there, or perhaps find Liora or someone else who might help me. I'm trying not to spend the 397 sim I have, since that's my mother's set-aside that I found and put back. The cost to move is likely minimal.

I'm thinking about my options once I arrive: maybe I can trade something, do a task for someone, or find someone willing to give me food. But I'm cautious - "cautious to a fault" as my character description says, and with money I think of it as a number, not a feeling. I also need to be careful about the time - classes start at the eighth hour (which would be 08:00 in this time system).

The cafe might have food available, and I can assess the situation there without immediately committing to spending the sim I have. Perhaps someone I know will be there, or there will be an opportunity to earn or receive food rather than buying it outright.  Two ticks to Hobbs Cafe. I can make it and still get back for the eighth hour, if I need to. If there's nothing there, if no one can help, if the prices are what I expect they'll be—then I'll have to decide. Spend what I shouldn't spend, or go hungry.

The sim in my hand isn't mine. I found it, counted it, put it back. That doesn't make it mine to use. That makes it something I know about that I'm not supposed to know about, and spending it would be like speaking the truth aloud when everyone's pretending not to see it.

I keep walking. One tick down, one to go. The cafe will have people, probably. Early risers, people with coin to spend, people with food to sell. I'll see what I can see, ask what I can ask, and decide based on numbers, not feelings.

Numbers I can trust. Feelings have a way of making you spend what you shouldn't.

output:
Hobbs Cafe, and nobody here. 396 sim now—another one gone to the cost of arriving. The eighth hour is forty minutes away. I came looking for options, and I found an empty room.

*But if...*

If Liora were here, she'd have food or know where to get it. If someone were working the counter, I could ask about prices without buying. If I had arrived earlier or later, maybe there would be people. If, if, if. The abandoned sentences pile up in my head.

I need to decide. Stay here and hope someone arrives with something to offer? Go back to the college and hope Liora appears? Walk to the bakery and see what Marta has, knowing I'll spend what I shouldn't spend?

The farmland is too far. The forest, the mine, the quarry—those are for workers, not students with empty hands. I have skills I learned at the college: studying, reading, writing, thinking. None of these fill a stomach directly.

The household pays upkeep tonight whether I eat or not. If I go home hungry, I go home hungry. If I spend here, I arrive home with less than 400 sim in my hand, and Mother will know someone touched her hiding place. Not that I spent it—she doesn't know I know about the 400 to begin with. But if I come home with 350 sim, or 300, or 200, and she checks her set-aside, she'll see the number wrong. She'll know.

I think I stay here. Five minutes, ten. See if anyone arrives. The cafe is for food and drink—someone must work here eventually. Someone must open, prepare, sell. I'll wait, and I'll watch, and I'll know what I know without saying it.

If no one comes, I walk back to the college hungry, and I sit at my desk, and I learn what I can learn until hunger makes me useless. Then I walk home, and I hope someone at the quarry has enough to feed me, or that Ainsley hasn't calculated exactly how much each of us is worth today.

The arithmetic of survival. I've done it. I know where we stand. I know what nobody is saying.

Thirty minutes gone. Cafe still empty. 

I need to get back to the college for the eighth hour. Missing class isn't an option—I need the college, need it more than breakfast, more than the temporary relief of someone offering me something. The future I want is past this town, past Kasukabe, past whatever becomes of quarry households that can't pay their upkeep.

I stand up. The walk back to the college is two ticks. I'll arrive hungry, sit at my desk hungry, learn hungry. Perhaps Liora will be there, and she'll have something, or she won't. Perhaps I'll find her absence as complete as her presence would have been unremarkable.

*But if she's not there, and if no one else...*

The sentence dies again. Hunger makes the abandoned sentences harder to complete. The body has priorities the mind can't override forever.

I need to move. Now, or I miss the hour. The cost of waiting has been paid; no one came. Time to pay the cost of walking back and see what the day holds.

I start for the door, for the path, for the college and whatever comes next.  I'm leaving Hobbs Cafe now. The walk back to Oak Hill College will take two ticks. I'll arrive just before or at the eighth hour, ready for my classes. I won't call any tools yet - I'm still standing here, thinking through the decision to leave. 

The hunger is real. I can feel it settling into my calculations, making each number feel heavier. 396 sim. Set-aside money. Mother's hidden 400, minus what I spent arriving here and arriving at the college, minus... I need to think about what this costs me, literally and figuratively.

But I don't speak thoughts. I only speak through the tool. And I'm not ready to speak yet. I need to decide: do I stay and wait longer, hoping someone arrives? Or do I go, accept hunger for now, trust that tonight at the quarry someone will have enough?

The eighth hour doesn't wait. I know this. I've walked to college for two years with Liora, and the hour comes whether we're ready or not.

I'm going. Standing up, walking out. The tool call will come when I'm ready to move.  Standing in an empty cafe, hunger pressing against my thoughts, and I know the arithmetic: wait longer and lose the hour I've worked to reach, or go hungry and keep what I've built.

I walk back to the college. Two ticks, same as coming. I'll arrive with time to spare, or time enough, or barely enough. The numbers don't lie even when people do.

*But if...*

But if Liora is there, if someone is there, if the day holds something I haven't calculated—

The sentence finishes itself in my feet, not my mouth. I'm moving. The tool will tell the world, and the world will know what I chose.

I didn't move. I stood here thinking, and thinking reached nobody, and the eighth hour has passed. I'm still at Hobbs Cafe, still hungry, still holding 396 sim that isn't mine to spend.

The college started without me. Liora, if she came, sat at her desk without me beside her. Two years of mornings together, broken because I couldn't decide between hunger and a number.

I need to move. Actually, this time. Not think about moving, not write about moving, but call the tool that makes the world know I've left.

Where? The college is where my work is, but class has started. I could still go, arrive late, sit at my desk with everyone watching. Or I could go somewhere else. The bakery. The farmland. Home, to the quarry, to face what I couldn't face this morning.

The household pays upkeep tonight. Bram, Ainsley, Tobias, Nell—they'll be there, and they'll know I'm hungry, or they won't, or they won't care. Ainsley especially keeps account of things. Of people. Of what costs what.

I should go to the college. Even late. Even hungry. Even with the walk there meaning another tick, another cost, another sim gone from the 396 I shouldn't be spending. The college is the path I've chosen, the only path I see past this town, and I won't abandon it because I stood still when I should have walked.

But first—this cafe is empty, was empty, will be empty until someone opens it or works it or owns it. I know nothing about who runs Hobbs Cafe, what they sell, when they arrive. I didn't think to ask. I only thought to wait, and waiting reached nobody.

I move to the college. Now.
